articles.title: Afghan cyclist who disguised herself as a man to evade Taliban wins Asian Games silver
articles.summary: Fariba Hashimi fled after Taliban returned to power. ‘This medal can show resilience from Afghan women’ An Afghan cyclist who disguised herself as a man to pursue her sporting dreams won an Asian Games silver medal on Tuesday, hoping it inspires other women in a country where Taliban authorities…
body: Fariba Hashimi, who is based in Italy, powered home second in the women’s road race near Nagoya in Japan, calling the triumph “something special”.

“I can’t explain my feelings now,” said the 23-year-old, before reflecting on how she was attacked with stones and trained disguised as a man when she started out in the sport as a teenager along with sister Yulduz, who is also now a pro cyclist. “I was born inside a country where the women who dream are getting attacked, and I’m really happy that I have fought against that,” she said. “I hope that the next generation will come here and represent their country without any fear.”
The Taliban authorities returned to power in 2021 and have since imposed a series of rules limiting women’s access to education and public life, including sport.

articles.title: Lions and Irons: the Dockers derby – a photo essay
articles.summary: For the first time in 14 years, Millwall and West Ham faced each other in their 100th meeting. Documentary photographer Adam Isfendiyar was at the Den to record the fans’ matchday experience. On 19 September 2026, Millwall hosted West Ham at the Den.
body: The two teams are separated and connected by the Thames. They were formed around the heavy industries of east London’s docklands in the late 19th century and were geographically much closer then – Millwall on the Isle of Dogs and Thames Ironworks, from which West Ham emerged, around Canning Town. Before Millwall relocated south of the Thames to New Cross in 1910, both were north of the river and only a little over two miles apart.

Now the Lions, Millwall were known as the Dockers during their formative years. West Ham’s nickname, the Irons, refers to their origins among workers at the Thames Ironworks and Shipbuilding Company. Dock work was precarious and physically demanding. Men could turn up each morning with no guarantee of being chosen for work, and competition for a day’s labour could be fierce. That world fostered ideas of toughness, loyalty and hard work which still form part of how both clubs understand and present themselves.

articles.title: ‘It’s bordering on exploitation’: how pseudoscience is duping football
articles.summary: Cryotherapy chambers and other practices have little evidence behind them, says top performance director. Dr Claire-Marie Roberts was working at Coventry City when she received a call from someone asking whether she knew how much oxygen was in the atmosphere.
body: “It is only 21%,” the caller told her. That’s GCSE chemistry, she thought. Then came the sales pitch: “So what we’ve done is put oxygen in a can and we think you might want to use it.”
“Right … oxygen in a can,” Roberts says, laughing at the memory. Suffice to say, she did not take the caller up on his offer to buy oxygen in a can for Coventry’s players.

Roberts has spent decades working in elite athlete performance and professional football, including nine years at the Premier League and two at Coventry, where she played a key role in their promotion as Championship champions before joining the Formula One team McLaren as director of human performance in the summer. She is shocked by how professional football is being duped by pseudoscience: from coaches and performance staff misled by snake-oil sellers, to players desperate for a shortcut and with money to burn.

“It’s the science-practice gap, which is widening in my experience,” Roberts says. “I think it’s getting much worse. There’s so much sparkly marketing behind all these things. It’s bordering on exploitation.

articles.title: Women’s Champions League: will OL Lyonnes or English trio topple a weakened Barcelona?
articles.summary: The league phase kicks off this week, with several sides optimistic of unseating the European champions. This competition is wide open. “But, wait, you say that every year!” No, honestly, this time it is wide open.
body: The Spanish champions, who have reached six European finals in a row, have had four players who started the victory in the final last season leave the club. Ona Batlle joined Arsenal, Salma Paralluelo signed for OL Lyonnes – against whom she scored twice in that 4-0 victory to clinch the title in May – and Alexia Putellas and Mapi León moved to London City Lionesses. They have a very different look and feel to the formidable aura they demonstrated in Oslo.

They are still the team to beat, though, and retain an excellent squad, including the winner of the last three Ballons d’Or in Aitana Bonmatí – although she is doubtful for their opener against Paris FC on Wednesday with injury – as well as the top scorer in the competition last season, Ewa Pajor, and their captain, the Spain midfielder Patri Guijarro.
It will still take a world-class team to topple them, but there is perhaps no longer that same air of invincibility accompanying them this time.

articles.title: Egan's late career resurgence back to Premier League
articles.summary: BBC Sport NI looks at Republic of Ireland centre-back's John Egan's rise back to the Premier League with Hull City and the international set-up under Heimir Hallgrimsson.
body: Just 18 months ago a 31-year-old John Egan was struggling for minutes off the bench for promotion-chasing Burnley and decided to make a January switch to fellow Championship side Hull City.
Fast forward to the present day and Egan is a Premier League regular for the Tigers, who have taken everyone by surprise upon their return to the top flight.

It's been quite a turnaround for the now 33-year-old, who probably thought his last Premier League appearance had already come, when he was taken off on a stretcher with a season-ending Achilles injury when playing for Sheffield United against West Ham in September 2023.
Egan has quietly rebuilt his career after being released by the Blades, first with the Clarets before finding a home at Hull after joining in 2024.

articles.title: 'This is not Wrexham. I'm not Ryan Reynolds' - behind the scenes at world's oldest club
articles.summary: A new BBC podcast Mud, Sweat and Cheers: Trouble at the Bottom – Sheffield FC goes behind the scenes on an extraordinary season at the world's oldest football club.
body: A football club at the heart of a tug-of-war between a Qatari-backed venture capital firm and a rock star probably isn't that unusual nowadays.
This is the position that Sheffield FC, founded in 1857 and widely considered the world's oldest football club, were in earlier this year.

Mud, Sweat and Cheers: Trouble at the Bottom – Sheffield FC, a six-part podcast series from BBC Local and BBC Radio Sheffield and hosted by Sheffield singer-songwriter Self Esteem, goes behind the scenes during an extraordinary season for an extraordinary club.

The Club, as they're aptly nicknamed given their historic place in the sport, helped to underpin many of the laws of the modern game with the 'Sheffield Rules' and are one of just two clubs to have been awarded Fifa's prestigious Order of Merit, alongside 15-time European Cup winners Real Madrid.

articles.title: 'His passing has left a big hole.' BJ Sigler remembered in Indiana baseball community
articles.summary: Ballpark lights illuminated the night sky across Indiana baseball stadiums on Thursday. Fields were lit up to honor BJ Sigler, the Jennings County High School baseball coach who died at the age of 50 on Sept. 10. Social media was flooded with tributes for the late coach. #LightsonforBJ.
body: Sigler was an advocate for youth baseball, whose influence was felt in every corner of the state and well past its lines.

“His passing has left a big hole in our community,” said Jennings County assistant coach Bill Lane. “He was a competitor; I think that’s the first thing anyone would you about him. But he was also generous with his time, resources and knowledge for the game.
“As a coach he believed in his players and pushed them to be their best. He had a tremendous impact on our team, our school, our program and he’s going to be dearly missed.”

Sigler, a 1994 graduate of Providence High School, played baseball at Indiana University-Southeast before he served in the United States Air Force. He launched the Panther Baseball Club, a travel ball organization based out of North Vernon, to help kids play baseball. Sigler covered costs out of pocket. It was a deed meant to create opportunities for the next generation of players.

articles.title: 'Alarming' - does WSL have a homegrown problem?
articles.summary: The London City Lionesses raised eyebrows with no English players in their starting line-up against Manchester United, but is there a wider trend?
body: When London City Lionesses beat Manchester United on the opening night of the 2025-26 season, it suggested times were changing in the English women's game.

For some, that had become clear about an hour before kick-off in Bromley when the team news revealed a starting XI without any English players - the first time a Women's Super League side had done so on the first day of the season.
Two days later it happened again, when Scotland striker Kirsty Hanson was the only British player to start for Tottenham in their win over West Ham.
Both instances speak to the increasing ability of WSL clubs to attract top talents from across the globe, creating a league many now view as the world's best.

articles.title: Why are Republic of Ireland playing against Israel?
articles.summary: The Republic of Ireland face a double-header against Israel in the Uefa Nations League, with their ‘home’ fixture taking place in Serbia amid calls to boycott the fixtures amid the conflict in Gaza
body: Ahead of the Uefa Nations League draw in Brussels back in February, the Football Association of Ireland (FAI) were already preparing themselves for the worst. With the Republic of Ireland sitting in Pot 3 of the League B draw, they knew one of their four potential opponents from Pot 1 posed a far greater political and logistical headache than the others – the true scale of which the FAI are facing now. The Republic landed in Group B3 along with top seeds Israel, as well as Austria and Kosovo. Within minutes, the FAI confirmed they would fulfil both home and away fixtures against Israel, neither of which will take place in Ireland, or in Israel.

A spokesperson from European football’s governing body said: “Decisions to avoid certain teams being drawn against each other are made taking into consideration several factors, especially conditions between the two countries leading to structural risks for security. Uefa handles every situation very carefully on its own merits and monitors all facts and developments.”

articles.title: 'Just getting started' - Pollock signs new multi-year deal with Saints
articles.summary: Henry Pollock has signed a new multi-year contract extension with Northampton Saints that will see him stay at his boyhood club beyond this season.
body: In a statement, Pollock said: "I'm massively happy to re-sign with Saints, my boyhood club. It's an exciting place to be right now. We're in a great spot as a team, but it feels like there's still so much more growth in us.

"I'm still young, and we've got a young squad with a brilliant group of lads. Some of my best mates are here, and every day everyone pushes each other to improve and be the best players and team we can be. For where I am in my career, this is exactly where I want to be.

"I feel like we're only just getting started. We won the PREM last season and we want to go again. Winning the Champions Cup is another huge ambition for us. We came so close a couple of years ago, and achieving that together would be incredibly special.

"I just want to enjoy every moment of this journey. I'm playing for my boyhood club, surrounded by great people, and that's something I never take for granted. The connections within this group are what make it such a special place."

articles.title: A mixed Ryder Cup-style team event - could it happen and how would it work?
articles.summary: Team events are some of the biggest weeks in the golfing calendar, but how realistic is adding a new mixed-gender golf tournament to an already packed schedule?
body: The Ryder Cup and Solheim Cup both see the best from Europe take on the United States, while the Presidents Cup - live this week on Sky Sports - is a biennial contest between Team USA and an International Team.

The Grant Thornton Invitational is a mixed team tournament taking place every December containing PGA Tour and DP World Tour players, following on from the defunct JCPenney Classic, but is there space for one on an international scale?

A mixed team golf event will feature in the Los Angeles Olympics in 2028, while Team Europe captain Luke Donald recently suggested launching a mixed team event that would share similarities with the Ryder Cup and Solheim Cup.
"I'm all for having some events where we're playing together and sharing each other's talents," Donald told the Telegraph ahead of the BMW PGA Championship. "I think it's great to see that.

articles.title: Wigan focused on taking on 'battle-hardened' Wakefield in semis
articles.summary: Wigan Warriors have been there, done that, and got the T-shirt when it comes to making it to the Betfred Super League Grand Final and so their routine is set as they hunt down the treble in 2026.
body: Wigan have already added two trophies to their cabinet this season having won the Challenge Cup and League Leaders' Shield, with the Grand Final just one step away.
To get there, they need to beat Wakefield in the semi-finals on Saturday September 26, live on Sky Sports after Daryl Powell's side defeated Leigh in the eliminators.
Matt Peet lost a first final as head coach of Wigan at Old Trafford in 2025 against Hull KR, but has already made sure that such heartbreak was fuel to achieve more.
But now, with success firmly in their sights once again, Wigan will keep looking forward while being rooted in the present and ensuring they are firmly focused on the semi-finals.
